decisions.executionNote: Approach the near side of the straightedge symmetrically while pitching grippers downward; establish safe elbow-up approach before contact.
Retry initial approach at smaller increments after zero-execution continuity rejection.
Continue symmetric downward orientation, keeping straightedge clear until tips are positioned behind it.
Close empty grippers to form push contacts and pitch further down; keep both contacts separated on their own side.
Bring downward-facing closed tips toward the straightedge's near face, with a small descent. Monitor height before pushing.
Test a slow level push through the straightedge with both closed grippers; avoid any lifting and watch for edge motion.
Straightedge rotated because left contact did not engage. Hold right side and lift/retract the left tip to reposition behind the lagging end.
Lower left contact slightly and advance the lagging end only, using the right gripper as a stationary guide.
Continue advancing the left contact alone to bring the straightedge closer to a horizontal row direction.
Square the tool by advancing the left side another small amount while holding the right. Blocks remain on the tabletop.
Left tip appears to slide over the edge. Reposition it back and down to match the effective right-side pushing height before further alignment.
Advance the repositioned left contact slowly until the straightedge is level, holding the right end steady.
Push the now nearly level straightedge toward the blocks with both arms, slightly equalizing the left edge. Keep cube contact strictly horizontal.
All three blocks are reaching the straightedge. Continue a slow planar push, advancing the right side slightly more to remove the small edge skew.
The three blocks appear straight and mutually parallel against the tool. Disengage backward and slightly upward without disturbing them, then reset both arms.
Withdraw both arms along their own sides, reopen the empty grippers, and begin restoring the original wrist orientation; aligned blocks remain untouched.
Continue smooth elbow-up reset toward the starting positions and orientation, remaining clear of the aligned row.
Reduce reset step size near the home configuration to preserve joint continuity; row remains visibly straight.
